headline: TAME reports improved VLM chain-of-thought monitorability with mixed capability trade-offs
summary: A September 21 preprint introduces TAME, which combines evolving prompt feedback with a targeted sparse-autoencoder activation penalty during reinforcement learning to improve the monitorability of VLM chain-of-thought. In experiments on Qwen3-VL-8B and Gemma-3-12B-it across GQA, VIRL-39k and SPA-VL, the authors report that monitorability can decline while task reward rises, and that targeted feature interventions and TAME partly restore their operational monitorability measure. A blinded paired human evaluation favors TAME on monitorability by 12.50 percentage points on VIRL and 13.75 on SPA-VL; two held-out monitor families also report positive changes on the same frozen traces. Task accuracy and general-capability effects are small or mixed and vary by setting. These are author-reported results; the operational metric does not establish faithful access to internal reasoning or better real-world safety.
